examples.en: Limescale has built up on the inner wall of the pipe.
Water is seeping out of the inner wall of the house.

examples.ko: 터널 내벽을 새로 칠하는 공사를 해요.
examples.en: They are doing work to repaint the tunnel's inner wall.
The inside wall of the pot got burned black.

examples.ko: 내벽이 얇아서 옆방 소리가 다 들려요.
examples.en: The inner wall is thin, so I can hear everything from the next room.

examples.ko: 보일러 내벽에 흰 가루가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There is white powder stuck to the inside wall of the boiler.

explain: 안쪽 벽면을 가리키는 말로, 파이프, 터널, 냄비, 보일러처럼 속이 비어 있는 것에 잘 써요. 반대말은 '외벽'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '안쪽 벽'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It points to the inner wall surface, and fits hollow things such as pipes, tunnels, pots and boilers. The opposite is '외벽' (outer wall). In daily talk people also say '안쪽 벽'.

examples.en: A computer has a cooling system inside it.

examples.ko: 자동차 엔진은 냉각이 잘 돼야 해요.
examples.en: A car engine needs to be cooled well.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 쇠를 물에 넣어 빨리 냉각시켰어요.
examples.en: I put the hot iron in water to cool it quickly.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 냉각 상태에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The relationship between the two countries has entered a chilled state.
The market mood has cooled at the moment.

examples.ko: 냉각 기간을 두고 천천히 다시 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's take a cooling-off period and think about it again slowly.

explain: '식히다'는 일상에서 음식이나 몸을 식힐 때 쓰고, '냉각'은 기계, 엔진, 과학 이야기에서 자주 써요. 사람 사이나 경제가 차가워질 때도 '관계 냉각', '시장 냉각'처럼 비유로 쓰여요. '냉각 기간'은 화를 가라앉히려고 두는 시간이에요.
explain_en: 식히다 is the everyday verb for cooling food or your body, while 냉각 is used more for machines, engines and science. It can also describe relationships or markets turning cold, as in 관계 냉각 and 시장 냉각. A 냉각 기간 is a cooling-off period.

examples.ko: 자동차 냉각수가 부족하면 엔진이 과열될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the car's coolant is low, the engine can overheat.
I had the coolant replaced at the repair shop.
The coolant warning light came on, so I pulled the car over.

examples.ko: 냉각수는 겨울에 얼지 않는 걸로 골라야 해요.
examples.en: You should choose a coolant that doesn't freeze in winter.

examples.ko: 냉각수 양은 보닛을 열어서 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check the coolant level by opening the hood.
Some power plants use seawater as coolant.

explain: 주로 자동차 엔진이나 기계, 발전소에서 열을 식히는 물을 말할 때 써요. 자동차 이야기에서는 '부동액'과 함께 나오는 일이 많아요. '냉각수 경고등', '냉각수를 보충하다'처럼 짝으로 기억해 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for the liquid that cools car engines, machines and power plants. In talk about cars it often comes up together with '부동액' (antifreeze). It helps to remember pairs like '냉각수 경고등' (coolant warning light) and '냉각수를 보충하다' (top up coolant).

examples.en: There was a leak in the ceiling, so I called for repairs.

examples.ko: 욕실 누수 때문에 아랫집이 피해를 봤어요.
examples.en: The people downstairs suffered damage because of the bathroom leak.

examples.ko: 수도관 누수를 막으려면 점검을 자주 해야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent water pipe leaks, you need to inspect them often.

examples.ko: 누수는 보통 벽에 젖은 자국이 생겨서 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can usually tell about a leak from wet marks on the wall.
I checked whether there is leak insurance.

examples.ko: 누수로 수도 요금이 갑자기 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The water bill suddenly came out high because of a leak.

explain: 건물이나 수도관에서 물이 새는 것을 말해요. 일상에서는 '물이 새다'라고 하고, '누수'는 집 수리나 뉴스, 보험 이야기에서 많이 써요. 가스나 기름이 새는 것은 보통 '누출'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to water seeping out of a building or pipe. In daily talk people say '물이 새다', while '누수' is common in home repairs, news and insurance. Gas or oil leaking out is usually called '누출'.

examples.en: Gas leaked out, so people went outside.
The company's information was leaked onto the internet.
The leaked oil spread into the sea.

examples.ko: 물이 누출될 수 있으니 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Water might leak out, so please check.
The pipes are old, so water keeps leaking out.

examples.ko: 시험 문제가 누출되고 나서 시험이 취소됐어요.
examples.en: After the exam questions leaked, the exam was canceled.

explain: '누출되다'는 가스·기름·물이 있어야 할 곳 밖으로 새어 나올 때 써요. 정보에는 '유출되다'를 더 자주 써요. 물이 새는 일상 상황은 '새다'가 가장 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 누출되다 is for gas, oil, or water escaping from where it should be. For information, 유출되다 is used more often. In everyday situations where water drips out, 새다 is the most natural.

examples.en: The wind was strong, so I closed the outer shutters.

examples.ko: 시골집 창문 밖에는 나무 덧문이 있어요.
examples.en: The country house has wooden outer shutters outside the windows.

examples.ko: 시골 가게 덧문이 이미 닫혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The country store's outer shutters were already closed.
In winter we put up an extra door to block the cold wind.

examples.ko: 덧문을 열자 아침 햇살이 방 안으로 들어왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the shutters, the morning sunlight came into the room.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 덧문은 열 때마다 삐걱거려요.
examples.en: The outer door at Grandma's house creaks every time it is opened.

explain: 문이나 창문 바깥쪽에 하나 더 덧대어 다는 문이에요. 요즘 가게의 내려오는 문은 '셔터'라고 많이 말하고, '덧문'은 시골집이나 옛날 집 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is an extra door or shutter fixed on the outside of a door or window. For a shop's pull-down door, people often say '셔터' these days, while '덧문' appears more in talk about country or old houses.

examples.en: It's an old house, so we redid the wiring.

examples.ko: 전기 배선이 낡아서 불이 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: The electrical wiring is worn, so a fire could start.
Leave the wiring work to a professional.
I covered the wiring under the desk with an organizer box.
We had it inspected to see if there was a problem with the wiring.

examples.ko: 천장 배선 때문에 전등을 옮기기 어려워요.
examples.en: Because of the ceiling wiring, it's hard to move the light.

explain: '전선'은 선 자체이고, '배선'은 전선을 필요한 곳에 이어 설치한 상태나 그 일을 말해요. '전기 배선', '배선 공사'처럼 집을 고치거나 전자 제품을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '선 정리'처럼 쉽게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: '전선' is the wire itself, while '배선' is the wiring as laid out and connected where needed, or the work of doing it. It often appears in 전기 배선 and 배선 공사, when talking about home repairs or electronics. In daily talk people may also say something simpler like '선 정리' (tidying cables).

examples.ko: 낡은 문을 열자 삐거덕 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: When I opened the old door, it creaked.

examples.ko: 계단을 올라갈 때마다 삐거덕 소리가 나요.
examples.en: The stairs creak every time I go up.
The chair creaked and then broke.

examples.ko: 침대가 삐거덕 소리를 내서 잠을 설쳤어요.
examples.en: The bed creaked, so I slept badly.
The front gate creaked open and Grandma came out.

examples.ko: 밤에 마루가 삐거덕 하는 소리에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled at night by the sound of the floor creaking.

explain: 문, 마루, 의자처럼 나무나 쇠가 서로 눌리거나 비벼질 때 나는 소리예요. '삐걱'도 비슷한 소리를 나타내요.
explain_en: It is the sound made when wood or metal parts press or rub against each other, as with doors, wooden floors and chairs. '삐걱' describes a similar sound.

examples.en: Running water has come to the country village too.

examples.ko: 상수도 요금은 두 달에 한 번 내요.
examples.en: I pay the water bill once every two months.
The water was cut off because of waterworks construction.

examples.ko: 상수도는 강물을 깨끗하게 만들어서 집으로 보내 줘요.
examples.en: The water supply cleans river water and sends it to homes.
A water main burst and the road was flooded.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 아직 상수도 시설이 부족해요.
examples.en: This area still lacks water supply facilities.

explain: 상수도는 깨끗한 물을 집과 건물로 보내 주는 시설이에요. 쓰고 난 더러운 물을 내보내는 시설은 '하수도'라서 둘을 한 쌍으로 말해요. 집에서는 '수도', '수돗물'이라고 줄여서 말해요.
explain_en: 상수도 is the system that sends clean water to homes and buildings. The system that carries away used dirty water is '하수도', so the two are talked about as a pair. At home people shorten it to '수도' and '수돗물'.

examples.en: The plastic touched by the flame shrivelled up right away.
I washed the sweater in hot water and it shrank.
The leaves on the plant are drying out and curling up.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 손가락이 오그라드는 것 같아요.
examples.en: On cold days it feels like my fingers are curling up.
Hearing that line makes me cringe.
When the air leaked out, the balloon slowly shrivelled.

explain: 열이나 추위, 마름 때문에 물건이 안쪽으로 쪼그라드는 모습에 써요. '줄어들다'는 크기가 작아지는 것이고, 이 말은 구겨지고 말리듯 오므라지는 모양이 핵심이에요. 요즘은 '손발이 오그라들다'로 민망한 느낌을 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 옛날에 쓴 일기를 읽으니 손발이 오그라들어요.
phrases.en: Reading the diary I wrote long ago makes me cringe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 민망하거나 낯간지러운 말이나 장면에 쓰는 말이에요. 실제 손발이 아니라 부끄러운 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for words or scenes that are embarrassingly cheesy or awkward. It describes a cringing feeling, not real hands and feet.

explain_en: It describes things pulling inward and shrivelling because of heat, cold or dryness. '줄어들다' just means getting smaller, while this word is about curling and puckering. These days it is often used in '손발이 오그라들다' to express cringing.

examples.en: I laid sawdust in the hamster's cage.
When you saw wood, a lot of sawdust comes out.
Sawdust is blowing around on the floor, so I have to clean.
In winter we stay warm with a sawdust stove.
Sawdust piled up high on the floor of the carpentry shop.
Sawdust is also used for growing mushrooms.

explain: 톱질할 때 나오는 나무 가루예요. 대패질할 때 나오는 얇은 조각은 '대팻밥'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 반려동물 바닥재나 난방 연료처럼 쓰임이 꽤 많아요.
explain_en: It is the wood dust that comes out when you saw. The thin shavings from planing are called '대팻밥', which is different. It has several uses, such as bedding for pets or fuel for heating.

examples.ko: 깨진 유리 파편이 바닥에 흩어져 있어요.
examples.en: Shards of broken glass are scattered on the floor.
Be careful not to cut your hand on the shards.

examples.ko: 폭발 뒤에 작은 파편들이 멀리 날아갔어요.
examples.en: After the explosion, small fragments flew far away.
I vacuumed up all the fragments.

examples.ko: 그 사건의 기억이 파편처럼 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The memory of that event remains like fragments.
Pieces of old satellites drift in space.

explain: '조각'은 어떤 것의 한 부분을 두루 말하고, '파편'은 깨지거나 터지면서 날카롭게 튀어나온 조각이에요. 위험하다는 느낌이 있어서 유리, 폭탄, 사고 이야기에 주로 나와요. '기억의 파편'처럼 흩어진 생각을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: 조각 is a general word for a piece of something, while 파편 is a sharp piece that flew off when something broke or exploded. It feels dangerous, so it appears in stories about glass, bombs and accidents. It can also describe scattered thoughts, as in 기억의 파편.
